text.p: Singapore police freed Associated Press (AP) reporter Vijay Joshi on Wednesday after he was detained following an altercation at a joint news conference given by British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind.
Singaporean Foreign Minister Shanmugam Jayakumar also took part in the press conference.
A police official said Joshi, an Indian national, would not be charged over the incident in which Rifkind's spokesman Nigel Sheinwald tried to intervene but was ignored.
In a written statement, a police spokesman said Joshi crossed the security rope barrier and "thrust his tape recorder towards the ministers in an overly aggressive manner".
The statement said Joshi refused to cooperate and became unruly when asked by a security officer to move back. Police took him into custody to prevent a further breach of the peace.
He was eventually released with a warning after the incident was investigated, the police statement said.
AP declined to comment on the matter.

A source close to Joshi told Reuters he was taken to a police station in handcuffs, told to write a statement of his version of the event and then waited for three hours before he was told no charges would be pressed.
The source said a Foreign Ministry official was present at the police station and appeared to have asked police not to lay charges.
Sheinwald told a plainclothes security official who pulled Joshi out of the ruckus around Rifkind that the reporter was not causing a problem, but was ignored.
